documents.title: Gateway release record
documents.body: The gateway release changed payment routing from the legacy pool to worker-b. Rollout completed before the observed latency increase. Timing alone does not establish causality.

documents.title: Latency observation
documents.body: Gateway payment p95 latency rose from 120 ms to 950 ms in the synthetic observation window. The measurement contains no root-cause assertion.

documents.title: Queue depth observation
documents.body: The settlement queue accumulated 420 waiting jobs. Its oldest job reached 85 seconds. Worker service time also increased.

documents.title: Worker B connection errors
documents.body: Worker B recorded connection-pool exhaustion while settling payments. A retry ceiling of three prevented unlimited replay.

documents.title: Pool configuration receipt
documents.body: Worker B used a pool limit of four connections after deployment. The previous configured limit was sixteen. This is a configuration observation, not a proven incident cause.

documents.title: Superseded cache note
documents.body: An early cache probe reported a healthy cache. This result was replaced by a corrected observation.

documents.title: Corrected cache probe
documents.body: A corrected cache probe reported degraded availability during payment routing. The early healthy result is superseded.

documents.title: Independent cache probe
documents.body: A second probe reported healthy cache availability during the same synthetic window. It conflicts with the corrected probe and requires human investigation.

documents.title: Connection investigation checklist
documents.body: Inspect pool saturation, worker retry receipts and queue age before proposing a configuration change. Publishing a dossier never executes a mitigation.
